c. K-MEANS CLUSTERINGSlide corrections ↗

EXAMPLE: CAFÉ CUSTOMERS

Use k-means to
group customers.

A café records how much each customer spends and how often each customer visits. K-means clustering puts customers with similar values into groups. Each group is a cluster.

THE CAMPUS CAFÉ

30 customers
2 features
One month of activity

Example data.
Not actual customer records.

PROCEDURE

Examine each step

Each small mark = one customer✚ = centroid
Feature scaling: The calculation divides spending by $200 and visits by 20. A $10 difference and a one-visit difference have equal weight. The axes show the original units.

Inertia —
K-means decreases the sum of squared distances.

Select the next step. To go directly to a stage, select its number.

Select a customer to compare the distances to all centroids.

TECHNICAL TERMS

SLIDE CORRECTIONS

Separate k-means from PCA

K-means does not select principal components. Principal component analysis (PCA) is a separate method. PCA combines the original features to create new axes. These axes describe variation in the data. They do not necessarily identify the features most important to the business. If the axes show spending and visits directly, use the term features.

SLIDE 01 · INPUT DATA

Prepare the data

  • Each point shows one customer.
  • The x-axis shows Feature 1: total spending in one month ($).
  • The y-axis shows Feature 2: number of visits in the same month.
  • Scale the features before you calculate distances.
  • Select K, the number of clusters. This example starts with K = 3.
  • K-means uses these features to put similar customers into clusters.
SLIDE 02 · THE ALGORITHM

Calculate the clusters

  1. Select K starting centroids. For example, select K customer points at random.
  2. Calculate Euclidean distances with the scaled features. Assign each customer to the nearest centroid.
  3. Calculate the mean of each feature for each cluster. Move each centroid to these mean values.
  4. Repeat the assignment and centroid update steps. Stop when assignments do not change or centroid movement is below a specified limit. Set a maximum number of iterations.

K-means produces K clusters. These clusters do not prove that K separate customer types exist. Different starting centroids can give different results. K-means++ is an alternative method to select starting centroids. Compare results from different starts and values of K. Use business requirements to assess the results. This example stops when assignments do not change.

References: scikit-learn · K-means · PCA
